articles.title: Golden State Warriors’ Kristaps Porziņģis steps away from basketball over undisclosed health issue
articles.summary: Warriors center, 31, announces decision on social media. Latvian big man does not disclose nature of health issue. Porziņģis leaves door open to return after long absence.
body: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health due to an undisclosed matter in a social media post on Friday.
Porziņģis did not reveal the nature of the issue in a message posted on his X account, and the 31-year-old did not make clear whether he will resume playing.
“I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn’t respond the way I anticipated,” Porziņģis wrote.

“I’m doing good, but I know what it takes, and I’m not where I want to be to perform at the level I expect from myself,” he added. “At this point, I’ve made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love.”

articles.title: Bad blood? Knicks defend Taylor Swift after players accuse her of being ‘fake fan’
articles.summary: Kolek calls singer’s courtside appearances ‘performative’ McBride agrees as teammates question celebrity fandom. Knicks give statement saying Swift is longtime supporter.
body: Taylor Swift’s love story with the New York Knicks caught an unexpected stray after two players from last season’s NBA champions accused the singer of being a fair-weather fan.
The Knicks released a statement on Friday defending Swift after Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioned whether the pop superstar was a genuine supporter of the team.
The reserve guards were asked during an NBA 2K livestream on Thursday to name the least authentic celebrity fan they had seen courtside at an NBA game.
“At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative because like they just want to be seen at the game,” Kolek said. “They’re not necessarily fans. Probably Taylor Swift.”

articles.title: Six tries and a big win - but were Ireland ruthless?
articles.summary: Despite a six-try and 30-point win over Argentina, Andy Farrell and Tadhg Beirne admit Ireland could have been more ruthless in Friday's win.
body: Before Ireland's Nations Championship game with Argentina, head coach Andy Farrell had been honest about where his side are less than a year out from the World Cup.

He admitted his team must improve if they are to challenge in Australia next year - a stark contrast to four years ago when they were riding the crest of a wave before they fell short in the quarter-finals.
Despite Mateo Carreras' early try, Ireland had far too much for Los Pumas in Dublin as they ran out 42-12 winners under the Friday night lights.
Hugo Keenan stole the headlines with his hat-trick, while Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher also crossed.

articles.title: ‘It was all of us’: Khawaja says entire Australia team knew about sandpaper ball tampering plot
articles.summary: Former Test opener says object also used on cricket ball in Port Elizabeth. CA remains ‘comfortable’ with bans only for Bancroft, Warner and Smith. Usman Khawaja has claimed “all” of the Australia touring party knew about the plot to tamper with the ball against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018…
body: The former Australia batter said the team used sandpaper to tamper with the ball before Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera while handling the object during the third Test, ahead of the release of Khawaja’s autobiography Sabr on Tuesday.

Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith were the only players sanctioned after a Cricket Australia investigation found the trio had prior knowledge of the scheme to use sandpaper as a ball tampering agent in Cape Town.
Captain Smith and Vice-captain Warner were suspended for 12 months for their parts in the plot, while Bancroft was handed a nine-month ban for using sandpaper on the ball.
“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” Khawaja told Nine newspapers.

articles.title: Thierno Barry double fires Everton to comeback win against Coventry
articles.summary: The wildly optimistic Evertonian – if such a being exists – could not have envisaged David Moyes’ side fifth in the Premier League with Thierno Barry just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart when their transfer window closed in calamitous fashion.
body: Frank Lampard endured a torturous night against his old club as Coventry impressed but were refused two strong penalty claims. The Coventry manager felt his team were denied a third time by the video assistant referee for an apparent handball by Barry when edging Everton ahead. Replays were inconclusive. It was the dancing French forward’s second goal of the game and 10th in all competitions this season. He also delivered a fine assist for Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall as the in-form midfielder put his latest England disappointment behind him to seal victory in convincing style.

articles.title: England 'disappointment' fuels Dewsbury-Hall's Everton heroics
articles.summary: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responds to his England omission by scoring a stunning goal to inspire Everton's 3-1 comeback victory over Coventry City.
body: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall let his performance do all the talking at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday night.

The Everton midfielder endured a disappointing start to his matchday preparations just hours earlier after learning that, despite his impressive performances in recent weeks, he had been overlooked by England manager Thomas Tuchel for this month's Nations League fixtures.
It was a setback for the 28-year-old, who was tipped to earn a place in Tuchel's latest squad but was ultimately left out, with Borussia Dortmund teenager Jobe Bellingham selected instead.
By the end of the night, though, Dewsbury-Hall had every reason to smile.

articles.title: WTA chair apologises to Pegula after 'diva' comment broadcast
articles.summary: Audio recording on practice courts will be deactivated at the WTA Finals after private comments made by Jessica Pegula about Mirra Andreeva were picked up, with the governing body's chair apologising to the American for the "regrettable" incident.
body: US player Pegula describing Russian teenager Andreeva as "a diva" while conversing with coach Mark Knowles during a practice session were heard on a YouTube livestream at Indian Wells, the venue for the WTA Tour season-ending event from November 8-15.

The WTA shouldered the blame for failing to properly inform players about active microphones, with chair Valerie Camillo saying there was "a lack of advanced notice and clear signage" as she confirmed audio will now be switched off for practice sessions.
Camillo added: "I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles. What happened was regrettable and unacceptable.
"Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction.

articles.title: Lampard: VAR didn't do its job
articles.summary: Coventry boss Frank Lampard says VAR 'didn't do its job' in his side's defeat to Everton as three reviews controversially went against his side.
body: Two penalty appeals and a possible handball for Everton's second goal were all reviewed by VAR officials Timothy Wood and Gary Beswick, but nothing was given. They were also not awarded on-field by referee Stuart Attwell.
Coventry opened the scoring after the two penalty appeals, but were ultimately beaten 3-1 on Merseyside on Friday Night Football.
Lampard told Sky Sports: "I hate to sound like a moaner. It's a football match and if you win the game, that can happen here. I've worked here and know the momentum swings in the game.
"I'm not trying to talk about the circumstances of the actual football, but when big decisions change games, they absolutely do. It's disappointing. VAR is there for that and it didn't do its job."

articles.title: 2026 ATP Finals Lineup Confirmed
articles.summary: After yet another grueling eleven-month-long season, we finally have the final eight players who will represent the cream of the crop of the ATP Tour in Turin at this year’s ATP Finals. Entering the Rolex Paris Masters, only four spots in Turin had been confirmed.
body: Alexander Zverev will head into Turin as the No. 1 seed for the first time in his career, having enjoyed a career-best season so far. Although the German currently has a below-average record of 3-9 against top-10 players, he has made the most of his opportunities, winning two Major titles and already securing the year-end No. 1 ranking.

A familiar face follows him in Carlos Alcaraz, who has now qualified for the prestigious end-of-year event for the fifth consecutive year. The Spaniard spent almost five months away from the tour this year due to a wrist injury, but despite that setback, he will finish the season ranked inside the top three. Alcaraz reached the final last year, and with his chief rival Jannik Sinner absent this time, he will hope to go one better.

American Ben Shelton became the next player to secure qualification for the ATP Finals. The American started the year inconsistently, but a career-best North American hard-court swing, during which he won the Canadian Masters and reached the US Open final, saw him climb the rankings and secure his place in Turin.

articles.title: Leclerc plans 'significant' car changes after tough day for Ferrari
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc says he will make "significant" setup changes to his car after "one of the worst feelings" in practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Leclerc was seven tenths off pace-setter Kimi Antonelli in second practice and Lewis Hamilton was nearly half a second behind as Ferrari trailed Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull on Friday.

It was a contrast to their recent pace with Ferrari claiming a podium position in the last four races but Leclerc is hoping they can turn that around in final practice on Saturday at 2.30pm and qualifying at 6pm, live on Sky Sports F1.
"FP2 was very tricky. Actually, if anything, one of the worst feeling I've had this year in the car, so there's plenty to work on, and it didn't feel quite right," said Leclerc.

"I've got some ideas. We'll change the car quite significantly, and we'll see how it goes. I hope we can do a step forward because even though I missed FP1, I don't think there was much performance in that.

articles.title: The rain couldn't stop Juanita Sanchez. Neither did North Smithfield.
articles.summary: Max Tuthill had a night to remember and so did Juanita Sanchez. Here's what happened against North Smithfield and what's next for the Cavaliers.
body: Max Tuthill has been the starting quarterback for Juanita Sanchez since his sophomore season and has flashed his athleticism and throwing ability. In the biggest game of his career – at least to this point – the senior put it all together.

As the rain came pouring down, Tuthill and the Cavaliers only played better. The offense put on a dazzling display in the first half and took away any doubt of the result by halftime before finishing off a 41-6 win over North Smithfield to advance to the semifinals of the Division IV playoffs.

“This is our first playoff win since I’ve been here,” said Tuthill, who attends Providence Country Day, which plays with Juanita as a co-op. “It’s a huge momentum shift for me and my team so hopefully we’ll keep going.”

Talent is something Juanita Sanchez has, but consistency is something its lacked this fall. The Cavaliers three wins came against two of the bottom feeders in D-IV, which forced them to beat Exeter-West Greenwich in the regular-season finale to make the playoffs.

articles.title: Four downs from Mason football's dominant district final win over Fenton
articles.summary: MASON — Here is quick reaction from Mason football recording its first shutout of the season with a 49-0 victory over Fenton in a Division 3 district final on Friday, Nov. 6. Player of the game. TROY PETERS, MASON: The junior added to what has been a big season with three touchdown runs.
body: Trailing 14-0, Fenton opted to go for it on fourth=and-4 from the Mason 15-yard line with just under 5 minutes to play in the opening quarter. The Tigers failed to convert a fourth down on the second straight drive — they had a fake punt pass attempt intercepted by Brett Camp — and Mason turned it into points when Gerrit Koot connected with Gavin Greathouse for a 22-yard TD with 1:39 left in the first quarter. That scored pushed Mason's lead to 21-0.

Mason captured its sixth district title in program history and fifth in six seasons with its latest victory. The Bulldogs improved to 10-1 and reached double digits in victories in a season for the fifth time. Mason now will have the opportunity to capture the fifth regional championship in program history when it travels to face Southeastern Conference White champion Chelsea next week. Chelsea (11-0) beat Redford Thurston, 51-14, in its district final Friday.
